title: Four ring operations for one constant-ring comparison
statement: Let (C,JC),(D,JD) be small sites, L a finite-limit-preserving functor of set-sheaf categories, and κ:constant_C ⋙ L ≅ constant_D an isomorphism natural in all sets [lem-route-inverse-image-constant-set-comparison]. Assume commutative-ring sheafification exists. Let A be any commutative ring, RI a commutative-ring sheaf on D, and e:L(|constant_C A|)≅|RI| compatible with the generalized-section graphs of addition, multiplication, zero and one (the record CategoryTheory.RingInverseImage, extracted unchanged from the parent module). Write κ_A^ring for the conjugation by constantCommuteCompose. Then for every U∈D, the function f_U=(e^{-1};κ_A^ring)_U:RI(U)→(constant_D A)(U) preserves zero, one, addition and multiplication. This is only a pointwise operation statement for one A; it asserts neither a ring-sheaf isomorphism nor naturality in A.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Identify the underlying constant ring sheaf with the constant set sheaf using constantCommuteCompose and its equation with the sheafification unit. On the constant set sheaf of A×A, the maps induced by the two projections give an isomorphism to the product of two copies of the constant ring set sheaf, since constant set sheafification preserves finite products.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: The maps induced by addition and multiplication, after the same underlying-set comparison, have sections equal to the sum or product of the two projection maps. Prove the morphism identities after precomposing with the sheafification unit; there they are exactly preservation of addition and multiplication by the ring-valued sheafification unit. Its universal property gives the identities globally.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Use naturality of κ for the two projections, addition, and multiplication to compare these diagrams after L. Apply the ringAdd and ringMul graph equations of e to the pair sheaf. The pair comparison, its image under L, and the finite-product comparison for L are isomorphisms, so every pair of sections of RI is tested. Conjugate by e to obtain the addition and multiplication identities for f.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: For zero and one use the constant singleton sheaf and its maps selecting 0 and 1. Naturality of κ for these functions and terminality transport their constant sections; ringZero and ringOne of e give the corresponding constants in RI. Conjugating gives f(0)=0 and f(1)=1. The argument imposes no nonzero-ring or nonempty-cover assumption.

lean.statement: theorem constantComparison_ring_operations {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D] (JC : GrothendieckTopology C) (JD : GrothendieckTopology D) [HasWeakSheafify JC CommRingCat.{u}] [HasWeakSheafify JD CommRingCat.{u}] (L : Sheaf JC (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JD (Type u)) (hL : PreservesFiniteLimits L) (kappa : constantSheaf JC (Type u) ⋙ L ≅ constantSheaf JD (Type u)) (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (RI : Sheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}) (e : RingInverseImage L ((constantSheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}).obj A) RI) : let f : ∀ U : Dᵒᵖ, RI.obj.obj U → ((constantSheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}).obj A).obj.obj U := fun U x ↦ (e.ringUnderlying.inv ≫ (constantRingSetComparison JC JD L kappa).hom.app A).hom.app U x ∀ U : Dᵒᵖ, f U 0 = 0 ∧ f U 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ x y : RI.obj.obj U, f U (x + y) = f U x + f U y) ∧ (∀ x y : RI.obj.obj U, f U (x * y) = f U x * f U y)
